points.description: States that the algorithm must be implemented (written as a program/code and run on a computer).

levels.says: Mentions running or testing the algorithm but does not clearly say it is implemented/coded as a program.

points.description: States that the actual (physical/wall-clock/CPU) running time is measured/timed, e.g. using a timer or system clock. Equivalent wording accepted.

levels.says: Says time is recorded but vague, e.g. 'observe performance' without clearly measuring time.

points.description: Mentions running it on various inputs (different input sizes/data) and recording/comparing the times, or analysing how time grows with input size.

rubric.notes: Full marks: implement the algorithm AND measure actual running time; the model answer's two ideas alone earn 4/5, and the fifth mark needs the input-size/varied-input idea. Part marks for vague versions. Counting operations or mathematical analysis (theoretical approach) earns nothing.
rubric.answer_key: Implement the algorithm as a program, run it on inputs of various sizes, and measure the actual physical running time (e.g. with a clock/timer), recording how the time varies with input size.

selftest_notes: The model answer scored only 4 of 5.
